data.description:
## Problem

Depends on 7775-46e5-3fd7-42d2, which replaces the spend cap's pricing-derivation
layer with a per-direction ceiling rate. That story changes enforcement. This one
supplies the three things that keep the change honest afterwards, all deliberately
separated so the enforcement change can land on its own.

**The test suite cannot currently catch the defect class being removed.** Its
fixtures synthesize rate keys from the ModelId spelling (`USE1-claude-sonnet-4-6-input-tokens`)
rather than the real billing label (`USE1-Claude Sonnet 4.6-input-tokens`), and
give each model one key per direction. So a label/id mismatch is impossible to
express, two co-resident keys for one model never occur, and no fixture carries a
snake_case usage type or a non-token metric. That fixture design is why 108 green
tests coexisted with four live defects, and it stays broken unless replaced.

**The ceiling's upper-bound property is an assumption with no monitor.** It holds
only while no model bills above the ceiling for its direction. A price rise or a
pricier new model breaks it silently, and the failure direction is the dangerous
one: the cap would fire late.

**The README documents the deleted design.** Its "How spend is measured" section
states prices are derived from the account's own bills, and enumerates a seed-rate
fallback order ending at `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`. All of that becomes false.

## Approach

Replace the synthesized fixtures with payloads whose *structure* is recorded from
this account, so the shapes AWS actually bills are present in the test corpus and
a future convention change fails a test instead of silently mispricing. Dollar
amounts and usage quantities are synthetic, because the code repo is public and
machine-local policy bars bill figures from it — structure is what the tests need.

Add a daily guard that compares the ceiling estimate for a settled day against
Cost Explorer for that same day and warns when the estimate falls below actual,
which is exactly the upper-bound invariant being violated. The guard only warns:
it cannot attach or detach the deny policy, so a guard fault can never cause an
outage.

Add per-model token counts to the warn and trip log lines only. Enforcement is
ModelId-independent by design; this is the diagnostic that answers "which model is
running away" without putting matching back on the enforcement path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A committed Cost Explorer fixture carries the structure of a real
  `get_cost_and_usage` response grouped by SERVICE and USAGE_TYPE, with synthetic
  amounts and quantities.
- [ ] That fixture contains a CamelCase usage type, a snake_case usage type, a
  `_Global` variant and a non-token usage type. Checked: a test asserting each
  shape is present, so the corpus cannot silently lose one.
- [ ] A committed `list_metrics` fixture carries every `AWS/Bedrock` ModelId
  series live on this account plus the non-token `SearchUnits` metric.
- [ ] No committed fixture amount matches real billing. Checked: a test asserting
  the amounts are the designated synthetic values.
- [ ] Every ModelId in the `list_metrics` fixture is priced by `CEILING` with no
  fallback path. Checked: a property test over the fixture.
- [ ] A daily guard prices a settled day with `CEILING` and compares it against
  Cost Explorer for that same UTC day.
- [ ] The guard raises an SNS warning when the estimate is below actual. Checked:
  a test driving an invariant violation.
- [ ] The guard skips days whose actual spend is below a floor, where the ratio is
  dominated by rounding. Checked: a test on a near-zero day asserting no warning.
- [ ] The guard cannot attach or detach the deny policy. Checked: a test asserting
  no IAM call on the guard path.
- [ ] Per-model token counts are logged on the warn and trip paths only, with no
  prices and no model matching. Checked: a test asserting the line on a trip and
  its absence on a normal tick.
- [ ] `infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/README.md` no longer claims prices are
  derived from the account's bills, and no longer describes the seed-rate fallback
  order or `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`. Checked: a test asserting those strings are
  absent from the file.
- [ ] The README states that the reported figure is an upper bound rather than an
  estimate of actual spend.
- [ ] The README states the accepted over-estimate for models cheaper than the
  ceiling, and the resulting effective-cap band in qualitative terms, naming the
  operator's local-only note as the location of the measured figures.

## Testing

Every criterion above is proved by
`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -q`.
`make lint` and `make typecheck` are the commit gate; `make verify` runs before
push per AGENTS.md.

## Rollback

Additive apart from the fixture replacement and the README edit, so reverting the
Gerrit change is sufficient. The guard warns only and touches no IAM, so it has no
enforcement blast radius; if it proves noisy it can be disabled by reverting alone,
without touching the enforcement path that 7775-46e5-3fd7-42d2 establishes.
data.title: Harden the ceiling-priced Bedrock cap: recorded fixtures, invariant guard, attribution logging, README
